# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# scenario: --scenario mismatch.
# NOT IN DESIGN.md §8's deliverable list; added by Phase 0 with its reason recorded in
# decisions/phase0-mock.md and tests/fixtures/README.md ("Additions"). The reason: §2a.9 names the
# test "the mock returns a tx_hash that differs from the built txid and the test asserts exit 1 with
# the entry still relayed: false", and NOTHING ELSE IN THE MOCK'S ARGV CAN PRODUCE IT. --fail makes a
# method answer a JSON-RPC ERROR, which is a different code path entirely (exit 5 or 16, not exit 1
# reason: txid_mismatch); --restricted only produces -32601. A successful relay_tx whose tx_hash
# disagrees with the build is reachable only from a second fixture, and --scenario is exactly the
# mechanism DESIGN.md §8 provides for a second fixture of one method.
# fields: identical to relay_tx.json -- COMMAND_RPC_RELAY_TX::response_t,
#         src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_commands_defs.h:970-977, one std::string key.
# THE VALUE is transfer-do-not-relay.json's tx_hash with its FIRST TWO characters swapped
#         (a1e7... -> 1ae7...): still 64 lowercase hex, still a well-formed txid, and different in
#         one byte. A wildly different string would also fail the comparison, but this one also fails
#         a careless prefix or suffix comparison, and it is visibly the same transaction to a human
#         reading the two hashes the error prints.
# WHAT A REAL DAEMON WOULD DO: never this. wallet-rpc derives tx_hash locally from the metadata blob
#         it was handed (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:1963), with the same function `transfer`
#         used (:1216-1221), so against a real wallet-rpc the two agree unless fmonero relayed the
#         WRONG ENTRY of a sweep's tx_metadata_list -- the one bug §2a.9's check can catch. This
#         fixture simulates the consequence, not the cause.
